claim_ceiling: This fixture qualifies deterministic environment mechanics and baseline sanity only. It does not execute Symthaea HDC, CfC/LTC, FEP, or an integrated HLB; it cannot support task-performance, SOTA, or consciousness claims.

environment.description: Partially observed binary-goal task. The agent receives a noisy initial cue and may pay a cost for a second noisy observation before committing left or right.
environment.random_generator: SplitMix64 with fixed constants, implemented in the Rust fixture
environment.information_boundary: The hidden goal and pre-generated probe signal are private environment state. The policy receives the cue and task parameters; the probe signal is revealed only after an Inspect action.

reference_policies.description: Commit to the maximum-likelihood goal from the initial cue; never inspect.
Always pay for the probe and then use the maximum-likelihood decision from available signals.
Inspect iff the expected increase in optimal goal accuracy from the probe exceeds its cost; then select by posterior likelihood.
Deterministic seeded random choice; independently has a 50% chance to inspect before choosing a side.

integrity_requirements: All policies receive the same scenario, world seed, initial observation, and action constraints.
The hidden goal is not part of the Observation type.
The probe signal is exposed only after a valid Inspect action.
Repeated inspection is an invalid action.
Fixed scenario and episode seeds must reproduce identical world observations and scores.
The perfect-information oracle is an upper bound only and is not a deployable baseline.
This fixture must not label a reference policy as the Symthaea FEP implementation.

research_context.relevance: Model-directed information selection and disambiguation of competing explanations.
Complexity-matched comparison; avoid assuming universal active-inference superiority.
